title: Five Millennia of Eclipses — historical-record schema
description: One JSON object per line (NDJSON) in data/records/<phenomenon>/<civilization>.jsonl. additionalProperties:false is the enforcement mechanism this schema exists for — a new top-level key MUST be added here (a reviewable diff) before any record may carry it. See data/records/README.md for the files and the keys that resolve outside the record.

record_id.description: Globally unique across ALL files, enforced by the corpus validator. Convention: <source-slug>-<phenomenon>-<NN>, e.g. xintangshu-tianwen-occultation-0390.

phenomenon.description: Also the directory a record is routed to, one per phenomenon. solar/lunar = eclipses; comet/guest/appulse/conjunction = transients. Replaces the old dual eclipse_type/phenomenon keys. conjunction (合聚) is several bodies gathered at one place — 「太白、辰星、歲星合于張」 — which the treatises record under their own headings (五緯合聚) and which is not one body grazing another; occultation would assert a subject and a target where the source names neither.

event_date.description: Extended-ISO astronomical-year date, in astronomical years (year 0 exists). BCE years are 6-digit zero-padded with a leading minus (-000762); CE years are plain 4-digit (0638) — this asymmetry matches the build's own date writer and every event_date value actually in the corpus, verified against all three pilot tables. Trailing -MM and -MM-DD segments are omitted at year/month precision respectively; see date.precision.

event_key.description: OPTIONAL hand-verified assertion that several records report ONE physical phenomenon. Records sharing an event_key are cross-highlighted together in the atlas rail and on the map. Write it only after identifying the records as the same object/apparition — it is an editorial claim, not a derived value, and nothing generates it. Solar and lunar records do not need it: their event_date is assigned from the computed eclipse catalogue, so date+phenomenon already names one event. Every other phenomenon takes its date from the source text, where it means only 'the day this chronicle claims' — two chronicles seeing one supernova date it differently (SN 1006 is 1006-04-09 in Songshi and 1006-05-01 in Meigetsuki), while unrelated sightings collide under a source-truncated date (a bare '1178' groups 96 distinct occultations). Neither case can be settled by date, which is why this key is explicit. Realistically it applies to supernovae and a few identified comet apparitions; it must NOT be used to lump occultations or conjunctions that merely share a day.

civilization.description: Must be a key present in data/concordance/civilizations.json. No record may carry null.

confidence.description: certain > likely > candidate. disputed/legendary are rare, hand-flagged. 'confirmed' is NOT a valid value — normalize to certain.

verbatim.description: The record's date as text_orig writes it: a stretch of text_orig copied character for character, from the first date word the date is read from to the record's own day, e.g. '閏二月庚辰朔' or 'gisteren'. What the source carries over from an earlier entry (the reign era, the year, the month) is not in it; the record's supplied tokens era=, year= and month= state it, and build/lib/han_dates.py reads the two together. A date word the source miswrites stays as written; an emendation note anchored in the stretch corrects it, and the reader and the supplied tokens follow the correction. Absent when text_orig writes no date of the record's own; a newspaper's issue date is source.locus.issue.

precision.description: How far event_date can be trusted. month precision => event_date's day segment is a nominal placeholder, not attested — see lunar_month for the source's own calendar month.

basis.description: Where event_date comes from. calendar = the source gives the date, in its own words or through its context (a reign era carried from the preceding entry, a newspaper's issue date with "yesterday"), converted by its calendar. canon = the source's date is insufficient and the eclipse was identified by matching the record against the computed catalogue (data/eclipses/*.json); this family is the one most in need of reading against data/records/visibility.json, since the matcher takes the global peak and never checks local visibility. scholarship = a scholar's dating is adopted. estimate = only an approximate time is known (mid-reign, a year).

epoch.description: Each year of a foreign era the text prints, as <calendar>:<year> (hijri:244), the calendar a key of data/concordance/calendars.json that counts years. js/notes.js (dateUnits) gives every place a translation prints the year the era's hover card, where the era's name does not already stand beside it.

hour.description: Each unequal hour the text prints, as day:<n> for the n-th twelfth of daylight counted from sunrise or night:<n> for the n-th twelfth of the night counted from sunset (canonical, Byzantine and Arabic reckonings alike). js/notes.js (dateUnits) gives every place a translation prints the hour a hover card with the modern clock hour it falls about.

verbatim_checked.description: The day verbatim was read against the base text and found to agree with it in year, intercalation, month and sexagenary day, while the sky contradicts the record (the Moon far from the lodge it names). The discrepancy is the source's own; the date stays as the source gives it. The check moon-far-from-lodge reads it.

lunar_month.description: The source's own lunisolar-calendar month number, for month-precision transients only (date.precision=month). Lets the shu'er (ear tab) records line show '五月' without fabricating a day. Cross-checked against date.verbatim by the corpus validator.

sky_position.description: The lunar-lodge / asterism position phrase as the source states it, e.g. '奎九度', '軒轅第四星'. Free text; not yet linked to concordance/xingguan.json.

key.description: Key into data/concordance/gazetteer.json .places, the sole authority on display name, coordinates, dynasty period and aliases. No per-record name or coordinate override exists: a site the gazetteer lacks gets its own gazetteer entry.

basis.description: How the place is known. named = the text names the site (for a newspaper, the dateline or body). capital = a court record that names no site, filed at the seat of the court. region = the text names a commandery, province or kingdom, and key is the settlement that was its seat in the period of the record. context = inferred from anything else (the chronicler's town, the paper's city). The visibility check tests named and capital records only: a verdict computed at a region's seat or at an inferred site tests the inference, not the record.

key.description: Key into data/records/sources.json .sources — the book/document this record is transcribed from.

locus.description: Where inside the source this record sits. Keys come from a closed vocabulary but their values are free text, because each tradition numbers its own divisions (卷052 / 卷四十七 / XVI / 40v). Only the keys a source actually uses are present. Each key's value is percent-encoded separately and substituted into the like-named placeholder of sources.json's edition.locus_url at render time, so a multi-segment locus needs no special casing. Assigned offline, claiming a juan only when the record's text_orig is found in exactly one juan of that book — never inferred from dates.

work.description: The CONTAINER: the individual work, when one source key bundles several (扶桑略記 / 百錬抄 / 吾妻鏡), or the periodical a communication ran in (Astronomische Nachrichten, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society) where the source key names only its observer. The title of the piece inside it is `section`, never here — a citation sets the container and the piece in different positions, and one key holding both cannot be typeset as either. Verbatim, never translated.

volume.description: 卷 / juan / Book / Liber / Tomus, in the edition's own numbering — '卷052' for 宋史 but '卷27' for 明史, '卷四十七' for 高麗史, 'XVI' for Scotichronicon.

number.description: The serial's own issue NUMBER, where it numbers its issues instead of (or as well as) dating them — Astronomische Nachrichten 33, Nr. 782. Bare digits: the unit word is the reader's, supplied per locale, because the German Nr. and the French n° name the same thing. `issue` cannot hold it (that field is an ISO date by pattern) and `chapter` would misname it, so a numbered serial had no home at all before this key.

chapter.description: 章 / cap. / ch. / §, the division below volume.

section.description: The TITLED PIECE inside the container, or a division named rather than numbered: a classical work's part (新羅本紀, 推古天皇紀), a newspaper article's own headline, the title of a paper in a periodical (Beobachtung der totalen Mondfinsterniß 1852 Januar 6 auf der Breslauer Sternwarte). A newspaper's standing department (LOCAL AND GENERAL., Échos, 漢口信息) is NOT a headline and goes in `column`: a citation puts the headline before the paper and the column after the date. A heading belongs HERE, not at the head of text_orig: one heading covers several records (EN PROVINCE runs over six Le Gaulois dispatches), which is what a locus is for, and a heading left in text_orig becomes the whole of the record's collapsed preview. Two decks of one heading join with an em dash. Verbatim, never translated — a citation does not translate the title it cites.

column.description: A serial's standing column or department, the named division the paper prints under the same name issue after issue (LOCAL AND GENERAL., GEMENGDE BERICHTEN., Échos, 漢口信息), with any instalment number it carries (Zaterdagavondpraatjes. — CCXVI). Cited after the issue date, 《申报》1882年5月22日，“漢口信息” — the 《历史研究》 newspaper rule — where `section` is cited before the paper. A piece that has a headline of its own under the column keeps that headline in `section`. Verbatim, never translated.

part.description: The numbered fascicle of a category whose name the source title already carries: 宋會要輯稿 cites 瑞異二之一 as the title's 瑞異, part 二, leaf 一. Written in Han as the edition writes it; the leaf goes in 'page'.

annal.description: The year-entry of a chronicle: 's.a. 840' is stored as '840', 'era MCCXXIX' as 'MCCXXIX', 昭公二十一年 as written.

era.description: The epoch 'annal' is counted from when it is not the Common Era: the Spanish era (CE + 38) or an anno mundi, Alexandrian (CE + 5492) or Byzantine (CE + 5508).

reign.description: The reign whose records contain the entry (憲宗實錄 in 朝鮮王朝實錄; 莊公 in 春秋經).

year.description: The regnal year within a reign (五年), used with 'reign'.

fragment.description: Fragment number in a modern edition of a fragmentary author: '122 West'.

page.description: Page number, only where the cited edition has stable pagination.

issue.description: The dated issue of a serial, as extended-ISO. A newspaper's issue date is NOT the record's event_date: the eclipse falls on event_date and the report appears in the issue of one to fourteen days later, so the two must be storable separately. Present only on serial sources; a book uses volume/chapter.

byline.description: The credit line printed in an article's head matter, above the report itself: the correspondent's byline ((De nos envoyés spéciaux.)), an agency credit, or a continuation notice ((Vervolg van Pag. 1.)). Head matter, like the heading it sits with, so it is cited rather than transcribed. Verbatim, never translated.

url.description: Per-record escape hatch: a link that neither edition.url nor edition.locus_url + locus can produce. Rare — most multi-volume sources are fully covered by locus. Takes priority over the locus_url template when present.

key.description: For appulse/comet/guest: the celestial object per data/concordance/xingguan.json .planets (moon/mars/venus/jupiter/saturn) or a comet/nova designation. Replaces the old bloated 'identification' block (212 distinct values collapsed to this + designation).

designation.description: A modern catalogue identification (comet/nova designation), where established by scholarship. Rare (18 records in the pre-migration corpus).

descriptors.description: Comet-specific observational attributes as the source states them: tail_length, tail_zhang, duration_days, colour, direction. Free-form (schema does not enumerate sub-keys — see README for the vocabulary seen in the corpus).

first_seen.description: ISO date the source gives for first appearance, when distinct from event_date.

end_text.description: Verbatim disappearance clause, e.g. '四十日滅'.

separation.description: How close the body actually came to the place the record names — COMPUTED, not recorded. Present only on occultation records dated to the day whose subject is settled and whose sky position the concordance can place; absent everywhere else, and absence never means far. It depends on the date, the subject and the sky position all having been read right, so it must never be used to revise object or event_date, which are where that evidence comes from.

deg.description: True angular separation in degrees, at noon UT on event_date.

uncertainty_deg.description: How much of that is ignorance: half the body's own daily motion, since the record gives a day and no hour, plus parallax where it matters. For the Moon this reaches some 4 degrees and routinely exceeds deg itself — a lunar reading below it says nothing about how close the body came, and a consumer must compare the two before treating deg as a measurement.

ruler.description: What it was measured to: the planet the record names as its target, the single star the record names, or the nearest member of the group it names; for a conjunction, pair: the widest pair among the bodies it names, with both bodies' daily motion in uncertainty_deg.

closest_deg.description: Least topocentric separation in degrees seen from the record's place, sampled every ten minutes through the local civil day, preferring moments with the Sun 6 degrees down and every body above the horizon.

event.description: What the computation, not the source, finds at that moment: occult = the discs overlap; appulse = within 1 degree of the disc's edge (for the Moon, a quarter degree out from the centre closest_deg measures); conjunction = the bodies gathered in one lunar lodge, or three or more across two adjacent ones; keep = an outer planet near its target within days of a station; apart = none of these. Names the event on the atlas slip.

bodies.description: The bodies in naming order: for occult the nearer body first; otherwise fastest first (Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn), with the Moon moved last in a conjunction. A single body means its target is a star.

star.description: For a star target, its entry in data/concordance/xingguan.json (asterisms.target_key): the HIP number when the record names a single star (毕宿五, 轩辕大星), else the key of the asterism the named part belongs to (毕宿右股北第四星 gives 毕宿). CJK locales show the entry's name; Western ones show the star's Bayer designation, else the entry's catalogue designation (M44), else its romanization (Bi).

unseen.description: No moment that day had the Sun down and every body above the horizon; closest_deg is then the least separation at any hour.

significance.description: LOD ranking hint for the map's marker-thinning selector. Absent = ordinary record. 'minor'/'routine' (old values) are simply omitted; prose values must move to note.

genre.description: OPTIONAL, newspaper-source records only: the editor's per-record newspaper subgenre (build/lib/genre_taxonomy.py). When present it overrides register.classify_genre, which reads only Western-language text and so leaves Han-script newspaper records unlabelled; 'editorial' has no text signature and exists only as a declaration. Absent = the classifier decides.

source_claim.description: What the SOURCE says about the sighting — one axis only, never what the sky permitted. 'seen' an eyewitness report; 'not_seen' the compiler says it was not seen without naming a cause; 'cloud' weather is named as the obstruction (陰雲不見); 'nonevent' the source says the predicted eclipse did not occur (當食不食). Absent = the source made no statement, which is the normal state of a bureau ledger line — do NOT default it to 'seen'. Whether the eclipse was observable from the place at all is machine-derived in data/records/visibility.json and must not be written here; a claim and a verdict that disagree is a finding, not an error to smooth over.

text_orig.description: The primary-source text verbatim, in its original script and language. The one field this whole schema exists to keep simple around.

translit.description: A romanization of text_orig (narrowed definition — NOT a place for source apparatus, machine boilerplate, or scholarly commentary; those belong in note). Present only for non-Latin-script originals where a romanization is meaningful and was authored.

text.description: BCP-47-keyed translations, one prose rendering of text_orig per locale. zh-Hans is authoritative and required; the other 6 are filled by the multilingual build pass (the validator's completeness gate: once any record has fr, ALL must).

supplied.description: Words a translation adds that text_orig does not write: the era name, year, month or day carried over from context, an omitted subject or object, or a word needed for sense. A word the translations print in the usual form is a token (era=hongwu, year=23, month=3, month=i4, subject=moon) that expands through data/concordance/eras.json, data/concordance/bodies.json and the ordinals of js/supplied.js; any other span is a written-out unit. The translation strings stay plain; the card wraps each listed span and adds the brackets (round brackets in Chinese and Japanese, square brackets in the Western locales). Checked by build/stage5_pack/validate_supplied.py.

notes.description: Editorial notes as typed units, each anchored to a word of text_orig, a header field, the source line or the whole record. js/notes.js renders them into numbered sentences in all seven locales from the note.* patterns of data/i18n/<locale>/ui.json and the concordance tables; the card puts a superscript at each anchor.

suppliedToken.description: A supplied span written as a token: era=<key> (the entry of data/concordance/eras.json whose k, or lowercased accent-free rom, is the key), year=N (the ordinal year of the reign), month=N (the lunar month; month=iN the intercalary one) or subject=<token> (an entry of data/concordance/bodies.json carrying that token). The token stands for the span of each of the seven locales and every one must occur in its translation.

supplied.description: One supplied span. text maps a locale to the exact substring of that locale's translation; {s, n} names the n-th occurrence when the substring occurs more than once before it. zh-Hant may be omitted: it is derived from zh-Hans by opencc.

note.description: One note unit: a type, a sub-case, an anchor and the slots its sentence pattern (note.<type>.<sub> in data/i18n/<locale>/ui.json) fills. Generated from js/notes.js by node tools/render-notes.mjs --schema; the format is documented in .claude/skills/assign-attributes/references/notes.md.
